⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files. <details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c385d3bd1642861a1cd681d71b78655ec1f75d7a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0e5473f595dea76b78f2fd7704cb4cedccefb427`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template + packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry-entry.test.ts

Inputs, read 2026-11-26T14:16Z: card #37549 (body and its 5 comments), PR #37557 (body, 5 files, net diff against `main` from merge-base `1af67b26cd`), and the 73 check-runs on the head: 61 success, 12 skipped, none failed, none pending. `main` is 11 commits past the merge-base and touches none of the files read below. The other three files of the diff (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.test.ts`, `ui/scripts/__tests__/doc-version-claims.test.ts`, the changeset) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; they were read for ①②③ and are not judged in ④.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Authorable accept set: unchanged. Right.** No Zod schema, error code, `authorable-surface/` baseline or `json-schema.manifest/` line is in the diff. The two template hunks add comment lines and two empty array literals.
- **Published surface of `@objectstack/spec/migrations`: declared types unchanged, values gain one own key each. Right, with the precise wording.** `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` and `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR` keep their declared type (a readonly record of number to readonly string array), and `api-surface/migrations.json` and `export-origins/migrations.json` are not in the diff. The generated value of each table gains `19: []`, so `Object.keys()` on either now lists `19`. The PR body's "no exported value or key changes shape" is true of the type and loose about the key set. No reader depends on the key set: at this head every reader of the two tables outside test files is in `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts` (`:841`, `:848`, `:1039`, `:2690`), each folding entries into a map or a flat list, where an empty array contributes nothing; the root `scripts/measure-partial-retirement-annotation.mjs` parses the table body as text and likewise finds no entry in an empty region. No `src` module of any package, `ui/` included, reads either table; the test readers index `[17]` or `[18]`, flatten, or loop the entries.
- **Build-time accept set of `gen:migration-registry`: widened on purpose. Right.** `renderRegistry` (`build-migration-registry.ts`) refuses an entry whose `kind:major` has no marked region. `19.*.ts` files under `entries/retired-keys/` and `entries/retired-defs/` were refused on every tree and are now concatenated. This matches `semantic:19`, open since the protocol move. An entry registered under 19 while the package is still 18.x cannot age out early: the deletion gate (`build-schemas.ts:2973`) computes 18 - 19, which is below the one-major age.
- **New red: the pin.** Any tree on which a kind in `KINDS` lacks an open or close marker for the spec package major or for `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` now fails `build-migration-registry-entry.test.ts`, in the spec `local` project that Test Core runs. Right; judged in ④.
- **Runtime: no product change. Right.** `clientSpecVersionVerdict` (`mcp-authoring.ts:203`) already validates with `SEMVER_2_0_0_VERSION_PATTERN` and compares only the first two dot fields of each side, which sit before any prerelease hyphen. The test now parses the way the door validates; the new case pins that a prerelease client saves against the same major and minor.
- **UI: the `KNOWN_CLAIMS` row follows the spec package major. Right.** That is the value `scripts/check-skill-compatibility-version.mjs --fix` writes into the skill's pin in the version step, so the row and the literal move together.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/37549-retired-key-19-region.md` grades `@objectstack/spec` `patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`. That matches what the diff publishes: the template renders into the `registry` module the `./migrations` entry ships, and the only shipped difference is two empty keyed arrays. Nothing an author writes against is added, narrowed or changed in meaning, so the level axis gives `patch`.
- The `Clause-②: no` line on the PR body and on the changeset holds: no accept-set narrowing, no new required member, no removed export.
- No changeset is owed for `@objectstack/runtime`: its manifest publishes `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, and the one runtime file in the diff is a test. `ui/scripts/__tests__/` is unpublished. Both `Check Changeset` runs concluded success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions` 1 (PR body covered only item 1): answered.** The body at this head covers all three items and names the dev report 7194227076; that is the dev's option A.
- **Dev flag "no L2 owed, seat decides": answered, owed.** `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template` is a non-test path under `packages/spec/src/**`, the schema face, at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. This record is that review.
- **Dev flag "pin majors differ from the dispatch order's current major plus one": answered in ④.** The dev's choice holds.
- **Dev flag "overlap clean, none of #37366 #37371 #37422 touches the template": stale for #37371, no conflict.** #37371 at `bad558d574` now edits this template (the `step19` doc comment, rationale and `conversionIds`, 10 added and 4 removed) and adds a `19.*` semantic entry. Its hunks sit in the `step19` block; this PR's sit in the two retired tables more than 150 lines below. Either merge order is textually clean, and #37371 adds no major-19 retired entry. #37366 and #37422 add major-18 semantic entry files only.
- **Declared local gaps** (`check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure` not measured; runtime suite narrowed to one file): covered by the head's check-runs, all success.
- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; nothing was written off the relay.
- **SQL push-down:** the diff holds no query, id materialisation or join. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`registry.ts.template`.** The contract is the generator's refusal plus the gate's prescription. `build-schemas.ts:769` reads `CURRENT_MAJOR` from the spec package version with `Number.parseInt`, which gives 19 for `19.0.0-next.0`. `renderNewEntryFiles` (`:828`) names every new entry file under that major for BOTH kinds: retired-key at `:1223`, retired-def at `:883` and `:2800`. The generator then requires a `kind:major` region for each. The new markers at template lines 3907 to 3908 and 4046 to 4047 are spelled exactly as the generator's open pattern and `closeMarker` read them (four spaces, the same comment form as the major-18 siblings), and each sits inside its own table before the closing brace that the check-mode fixtures anchor on. The failing case on #35129 writes the file names check (b) prints into a sandbox copy and runs the sandbox's generator; with `retired-key:19` present the refusal it hit has no path left.

- **`retired-def:19` in place: justified.** Same root cause through the same function, same file, no behaviour. It stayed latent only because the def-side check-mode tests seed the table by substitution and never run the generator on a `19.*` def file; the first whole-def removal on the 19 tree would have met the identical refusal. The pin, uniform over `KINDS`, also could not go green without it.
- **The two new template comments** state what the code does: `PROTOCOL_VERSION` reads 19, `check:authorable-surface` is `build-schemas.ts --check`, and the manifest deletion gate prescribes under the package major.
- **Limit of the evidence.** Every check-run on this head ran with the package at 18.6.0, so none exercised the 19 tree. The 19-tree result rests on the static reading above and on the dev's uncommitted local run in the report; the real witness is #35129 once it is refreshed onto a `main` that carries this.

**`build-migration-registry-entry.test.ts` (the pin).** Tried against four trees:

- `main` before the fix (package 18, protocol 19): requires 18 and 19 for three kinds; `retired-key:19` and `retired-def:19` are absent at the merge-base, so two cases red. Agrees with the dev's ablation.
- This head: all six regions present, green (Test Core success).
- The Version tree (package 19, protocol 19): the set collapses to 19 alone, green. "Package major plus one" would demand 20 there and red the release tree, and a `semantic:20` region cannot be opened ahead of time without a `step20` in `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR`, which is behaviour. The dev's choice of `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` is the right second major.
- The next major: `PROTOCOL_VERSION` moves to 20 in an ordinary PR while the package is 19.x (the ruled route, admitted by `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` in pre mode with a pending major). The pin reds that PR until all three major-20 regions exist. That is the card's "fails on `main` when `PROTOCOL_VERSION`'s major has no region".

The import of `./build-migration-registry` runs nothing (the `invokedDirectly` guard, pinned by the first `describe` of the same file). The package-major read is the same expression as `build-schemas.ts:769`. The "reads two real majors" case stops a `NaN` major from passing vacuously.

- N1 (nit) — the pin's lead on the next major exists only on the route where the protocol constant moves first. `scripts/sync-protocol-version.mjs` still moves the constant inside the version pass when it has not moved; on that route both majors change together and the missing region first reds on the Version tree, as it did here, though now with a message naming the region. The changeset's "caught on `main` rather than on the Version PR" is true of the ruled route only. Accepted deviation: no second major covers the sync route without opening a step early (see the release.yml note below for the route that would).
- N2 (nit) — the pin spells the open and close marker lines itself, a second copy of the shape `renderRegistry` reads. Today the two agree and a drift could only red falsely. Driving `renderRegistry` over the template with one synthetic entry per kind and major would make the generator the judge. Accepted deviation.

**Out of the diff, read and not reviewed:**

- `.github/workflows/release.yml:825` — the post-version validation renders the post-version tree on a schedule and runs a fixed gate list; from the spec package it runs `protocol-version.test.ts` alone. All three of this card's failures are red only on that tree and none of their files is in the list, the new pin included. Adding the pin (one file, no build) there would cover the sync route N1 names. A follow-up card for the lane, not a change to this head.
- `mcp-authoring.ts:206` — the non-SemVer refusal text carries the literal example `18.6.0`; on the 19 line it names the previous major.
- `build-schemas.ts:769` — on `main` today the gate prescribes `18.*` entry names while `PROTOCOL_VERSION` reads 19 and the 19 regions are open. Which major a retirement merged in this window belongs to is decided there; this PR does not change it.
- `doc-version-claims.test.ts` (remainder) — `workspaceRoot()` returns the objectui root in the standalone layout, where `packages/spec/package.json` does not exist, so the new module-scope read would throw there. The row it serves already presumes the monorepo (the skill lives in the root `skills/`).

**VERDICT: PASS**
